solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Find fault, whether there's good in it or not

definitions.text: Find fault, whether there's good in it or not

indicators.note: the phrase says the letter for good is placed inside the word for complaining

parts.note: to find fault is to whine or complain

explanation.surface: A grumble about whether something has any merit in it at all.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue works both ways: WHINE and the answer both mean find fault, and the answer is WHINE with G put 'in it'; with good or not, the meaning is the same.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to grumble or complain persistently is to find fault.

clue.text: Bird painter

definitions.meaning: a ... is any of various birds, such as the golden ... of Australia
James McNeill ..., the American-born painter of '... Mother'

explanation.surface: A painter of birds.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is an Australasian songbird, the other the famous nineteenth-century artist.

clue.text: Lilo is in a decomposed state

indicators.note: broken down into parts, so the letters of the words before it are put into a new order

explanation.surface: A lilo, an inflatable mattress, lying rotted and punctured.
explanation.walkthrough: 'state' looks like part of 'decomposed state' but is the definition; 'a' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: one of the fifty constituent states of the USA, in the Midwest.

clue.text: Unafraid to stand up to trained fighter

parts.note: game means brave or willing, as in 'game for anything'
to cock is to raise or set upright, as a dog cocks its ears

explanation.surface: Someone brave enough to confront a skilled boxer.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a cockerel bred and trained for cockfighting.

clue.text: Crab teas prepared for pandas

indicators.note: the words are made ready in a different form, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Crab-flavoured tea made up as food for pandas at the zoo.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: red pandas, and also binturongs, are known by this name.

clue.text: Story written up — editor in high spirits

indicators.note: in a down clue, written up means the word is entered bottom to top, so read backwards

parts.note: a tale is a story

explanation.surface: An editor delighted once a story is written up for the paper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'written up' is the reversal signal; the dash is just punctuation, and 'in high spirits' must be read as the whole definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: being thrilled or overjoyed is being in high spirits.

clue.text: A horseman put out is an aggressive person

indicators.note: put out of place, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: a rider is someone on horseback

explanation.surface: A rider who has been annoyed turns hostile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put out' looks like annoyed but shuffles A and RIDER, ARIDER, into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an attacker who makes an incursion or a sudden assault.

clue.text: Parasites identified by a doctor on Lincoln's back

definitions.note: plural in the clue against a singular answer; the clue loosely uses the general class

parts.note: MO is a medical officer
Abe is the familiar name of US president Abraham Lincoln

explanation.surface: A doctor finds parasites on the back of someone named Lincoln.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' looks like a body part but reverses ABE to EBA.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: some single-celled amoebic organisms live as parasites, causing amoebic dysentery.

clue.text: Wine one is mistaken to be diffident about?

indicators.note: the word for shy goes round the other piece

parts.note: shy means diffident or lacking confidence
to err is to be mistaken

explanation.surface: A wine about which one feels too shy to be sure of oneself.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a fortified wine from the Jerez region of Spain.

clue.text: How the poet might brighten up at work

definitions.text: How the poet might brighten up at work

parts.words: How the poet might brighten up at work
parts.note: poets use an archaic shortened form of illuminate for brighten

explanation.surface: A poet trying to cheer up while writing.
explanation.definitionFit: Archaic or poetic verb: to light up or illuminate, as poets write it.

clue.text: Scot returned with one single undergarment

indicators.note: sent back, so the word for a Scot is read backwards

parts.note: Mac is a familiar way to address a Scotsman
I is the Roman numeral one
sole means single or only

explanation.surface: A Scotsman comes home with only one item of underwear.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a loose sleeveless top worn under clothing.

clue.text: If you are run down they will pick you up

definitions.text: If you are run down they will pick you up

parts.words: If you are run down they will pick you up
parts.note: sounds like ambulance crews collecting an accident victim, but means restoratives that lift a tired person

explanation.surface: Run over by a car, you are collected by rescuers.
explanation.definitionFit: Restorative medicines or drinks that give a pick-me-up to someone feeling weak.

clue.text: Don't forget about the constituent

parts.note: re means about or concerning
a member is a constituent part of a group

explanation.surface: A reminder not to forget the voter in one's electorate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'constituent' suggests a voter but means a component part.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to keep something in mind is not to forget it.

clue.text: He should be fair, but he doesn't play the game

definitions.text: He should be fair, but he doesn't play the game

parts.words: He should be fair, but he doesn't play the game
parts.note: not playing the game usually means cheating, but here a match official simply does not take part

explanation.surface: A complaint about someone who ought to be fair but cheats.
explanation.definitionFit: The match official must be impartial and is not one of the players.

clue.text: Made one in a short day

definitions.meaning: to marry is to make two people one

explanation.surface: Married within a single brief day.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is joined in marriage, the other the abbreviated midweek day.

clue.text: Show girl goes round in a hundred

indicators.note: the girl's name encircles the other letters

parts.note: Eve is a girl's name
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: A showgirl goes round a hundred times in a performance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Show girl' reads as one word; 'Show' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to reveal or display a quality is to show it.

clue.text: Object and don't go on

definitions.meaning: an object is an aim or purpose

explanation.surface: Raise an objection and stop talking.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is a goal or purpose, the other to stop or conclude.

clue.text: Dog used in security

indicators.note: the letters are found used within the word that follows

explanation.surface: A guard dog employed by a security firm.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a mongrel or worthless dog.

clue.text: High on joints in wild party

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece placed on another comes after it

parts.note: knees are joints of the leg
up means high, as in up in the air

explanation.surface: Someone high on drugs at a riotous party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'joints' hints at cannabis but means knees. A knees-up is a British term for a lively, noisy party.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a British informal term for a boisterous celebration with dancing.

clue.text: Sort of table used by chemists from time to time

definitions.text: Sort of table used by chemists
definitions.meaning: the chart of elements arranged by atomic number

explanation.surface: Chemists consult a table every so often.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense names the table of elements, the other means occasional or recurring.

clue.text: A delicacy that is consumed by obscure artists

indicators.note: the abbreviation is swallowed inside the word for obscure

parts.note: to fog is to obscure
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is
RAs are Royal Academicians, members of the Royal Academy of Arts

explanation.surface: A fancy dish eaten by little-known painters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'obscure' looks like an adjective for the artists but is the verb FOG.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: fattened duck or goose liver is a luxury food.

clue.text: Rises to announce the exhibition's ready for opening?

definitions.text: to announce the exhibition's ready for opening?
definitions.meaning: read as a trade-fair stand being up, i.e. built

explanation.surface: Someone gets up to declare an exhibition open.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is gets up on one's feet; the other playfully reads a display stand as erected.

clue.text: Still requiring an answer

explanation.surface: Something that remains in need of a reply.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is laboratory distilling glassware, the other a quick, witty reply.

clue.text: Not a precious stone, but possibly worn

definitions.text: Not a precious stone, but possibly worn

parts.words: Not a precious stone, but possibly worn
parts.note: worn suggests jewellery, but this is a common stone smoothed and worn by water

explanation.surface: A cheap stone someone might still wear as jewellery.
explanation.definitionFit: A small stone, rounded and worn smooth by water, of no value.

clue.text: Come back after hitting bottom

parts.note: sounds like recovering from a personal low, but describes a ball rebounding off the ground

explanation.surface: Recovering after reaching one's lowest point.
explanation.definitionFit: To rebound or spring back, as a ball does off a floor.

clue.text: It goes amiss to be a selfish type

indicators.note: going amiss means going wrong, so the letters are put in a wrong order

explanation.surface: Things go wrong when you are self-centred.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: someone preoccupied with themselves.

clue.text: It comes from the elver

indicators.note: the letters are taken out of the words that follow

explanation.surface: A young fish grows into an adult.
explanation.walkthrough: An elver is a young eel, so the adult comes from it in both senses.
explanation.definitionFit: The adult fish into which an elver grows.

clue.text: What people who had designs on eating out did?

definitions.text: What people who had designs on eating out did?

parts.words: What people who had designs on eating out did?
parts.note: having designs suggests plotting a meal out, but means engravers whose acid ate pictures into plates

explanation.surface: What schemers who planned a restaurant dinner did.
explanation.definitionFit: Engravers cut designs by letting acid eat into metal plates.

clue.text: When alone, get changed and stretch out

indicators.note: altered, so the letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: Once you are by yourself, you change and relax at full length.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to lengthen or extend.

clue.text: Pigs can't fly, but one pig might make it

definitions.text: Pigs can't fly, but one pig might make it

indicators.note: the letters of the words could be made into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Pigs may not fly, but a single pig could manage it.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface plays on 'pigs might fly'; the anagram of ONE PIG gives a bird that can.
explanation.definitionFit: A bird that can fly, unlike a pig.

clue.text: Chelsea versus Bath?

parts.note: looks like a football or rugby match, but Chelsea and Bath are both kinds of sweet bun

explanation.surface: A sports fixture between a London football club and a rugby town.
explanation.walkthrough: A Chelsea bun and a Bath bun are British sweet buns. The answer is also a British term for a noisy tea party or squabble.
explanation.definitionFit: A clash between buns, read literally; also a tea party or petty squabble.

clue.text: Thinks a great deal of modern day raw materials

parts.note: AD, anno Domini, marks the modern era
ores are raw materials from which metal is extracted

explanation.surface: Someone who values modern-day raw materials highly.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to love or admire someone greatly.

clue.text: There's a regular stream at day's end

parts.note: even means regular or uniform
a tide is a stream or current of water

explanation.surface: A river flowing steadily as evening falls.
explanation.definitionFit: Poetic word for evening, the close of the day.

clue.text: Poor cast at university — performs awkwardly

indicators.note: poorly arranged, so the letters are reordered

parts.note: up means in residence at university, as in up at Oxford

explanation.surface: A weak university drama cast acts clumsily.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: to misbehave or malfunction, causing trouble.
